h: The Torah’s Promise Heals the Past and Protects the Future

p: In the Pesikta d'Rav Kahana (the new edition, 19:3):
It is the way of a man to have compassion:
and it is the way of a mother to console:
כְּאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אִמּוֹ תְּנַחֲמֶנּוּ (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, יג)
'As a man whom his mother consoles' (Yeshayahu 66:13).
I will do what a father does and what a mother does, etc.
'I, I am He Who consoles you.'"
here only "Who consoles you" is mentioned,
to save the son from harm going forward;
to console him from the sorrow
that has passed over him until today.
And this is the meaning of "Anochi, Anochi":
this is the event at Sinai."
אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א רב, א)
it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 202a):
and this is "As a father has compassion," etc.
And consolation for what has passed,
that is, to rectify the corruption,
and in the Midrash Rabbah (Tetzaveh, Shemos Rabbah 38:4):
And this is what the prophet said:
"I, I am He Who consoles you"
"as a man whom his mother consoles."
And so too for the future:
Torah study was implanted in their hearts
and the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts;
and this is "as a father has compassion on his children."
that is, up to the root,
as is written (Idra Zuta, Zohar III 290a):
are the aspect of HaKadosh Baruch Hu and His Shechinah;
that is, the aspect of the Written Torah,
and I created Torah as its antidote";
and this is what it says:
is the aspect of Malchus, the mouth
we call it Torah she'b'al peh
"as a man whom his mother consoles."

p: And afterward it says in the Pesikta:
and wrote her a generous kesubah, etc.;
he left her and went off
to a land across the sea, etc.
the king returned from across the sea
were it not for the generous kesubah
So the nations of the world
וְנוֹטְלִין סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וְקוֹרִין (וַיִּקְרָא כו, ט)
and take a Sefer Torah and read (Vayikra 26:9):
and establish My covenant with you,'
Tomorrow, when the End comes, etc.,
Were it not for the Sefer Torah
that You wrote for us, etc.
And this is as is written
I would have perished in my affliction.'"
Now this needs to be understood:
"And I will turn to you," etc.
"If you walk in My statutes," etc.;
but when Yisrael are in exile,
it is when it is the opposite:
"And if you do not listen," etc.;
"If you walk in My statutes," etc.,
What does it come to teach us?
Would this be the reward for the mitzvos
that He would turn His face
that is, if the words of Torah
"and I will turn to you," etc.
And this is why it does not say
which is a more particular expression,
that is, in words of Torah in quantity;
in words of Torah in quality;
points up to the aspect of Atika;
to the words of Torah of Mashiach,
as it says in the Midrash (Koheles Rabbah 2:1):
that you learn in this world
compared to the Torah of the World to Come."
that is, that the holiness will remain
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 93a):
and this is the generous kesubah
And this is what it says:
to be saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara;
and likewise "Were not Your Torah my delight,
I would have perished in my affliction"
And this is what it says:
they will be saved from the yetzer hara;
that in the end you will listen.
